title: Dower (Denmohor) and Maintenance Claims in Bangladesh: How to Claim from Abroad
metaTitle: Dower (Denmohor) & Maintenance Claim in Bangladesh from Abroad
metaDescription: How to claim denmohor (dower) and maintenance in Bangladesh while living abroad: Family Court filing, evidence, limitation, enforcement and common defences.
heroIntro: Dower (denmohor) is the wife's right under a Muslim marriage contract, and maintenance is the husband's duty to support wife and children. When the husband or wife lives abroad, these claims are often ignored or delayed, but they remain enforceable in the Family Court. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Dower & Maintenance Basics
points: Dower (denmohor) is a debt owed by the husband; it may be prompt (payable on demand) or deferred (on divorce or death).
Claims are filed in the Family Court under the Family Courts Ordinance 1985.
Maintenance covers the wife during marriage and iddat, and children until they can support themselves.
A wife or husband abroad can sue or defend with an attested Power of Attorney.
Judgments can be executed against bank accounts, salary and property in Bangladesh.

toc: Common Defences and How to Counter Them

sections.content:
Under Muslim law, the Kabinnama records the amount of dower. The wife is entitled to it as a debt, and in the absence of an express term, the prompt portion can be demanded at any time. The deferred portion is payable on divorce or the husband's death. Unpaid dower is a first charge on the estate. Even if the wife waives dower in a Khula, the waiver must be clear and voluntary.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

• Wife: during the marriage, and during the iddat period after divorce (generally three months or until delivery if pregnant), under Section 9 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 and the Family Courts Ordinance.
  • Children: sons until they can earn a living and daughters until marriage; the father's duty continues after divorce.
  • Parents: adult children must maintain needy parents.

1. Collect the Kabinnama, NID/passport, proof of residence and evidence of non-payment.
  2. Calculate the dower owed and a reasonable maintenance figure based on the husband's income and the family's standard of living.
  3. File a plaint in the Family Court of the area where the wife lives or where the marriage took place.
  4. The court first attempts mediation, then hears evidence.
  5. Ask for interim maintenance during the case.

The Family Court ordinarily decides cases in a limited time frame, although delays are common.

If you are the wife in Bangladesh, you can sue a husband living abroad. Summons can be served through his Bangladesh address, by post, or by substituted service. If you are abroad, appoint an advocate by a Power of Attorney (see PoA guide) and a representative who can attend. Courts can accept evidence by video in many cases.

After a decree, the court can attach bank accounts, salary, property or shares, and may issue a warrant of arrest for non-payment. If the husband owns property in Bangladesh, you can ask the court to attach and sell it. Enforcement abroad is harder, so ask your advocate about reciprocal arrangements in the husband's country.

sections.h2: Common Defences and How to Counter Them
sections.content:
• "Dower was paid in cash." The husband must prove payment with evidence; a signed receipt or witness statement matters.
  • "She waived the dower." The waiver must be voluntary and proved.
  • "The wife left without cause." The court examines the facts; desertion by the husband or cruelty may justify the wife's departure.
  • "I have no income." Courts consider earning capacity, not only present income.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

faqs.question: Can a wife claim denmohor after many years?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to limitation rules; deferred dower is generally payable on divorce or death, and the limitation period usually runs from that event.

faqs.question: Can I claim maintenance from a husband abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the Family Court, with service of summons and enforcement against his assets in Bangladesh.

faqs.question: Does a wife who takes Khula lose her dower?
faqs.answer: Usually the wife gives up her dower or part of it as consideration, but the terms must be clear and voluntary.

faqs.question: How long does a Family Court take?
faqs.answer: The law sets short targets, but practical delays are common. Interim orders can help during the case.

faqs.question: Is dower inherited?
faqs.answer: Yes. Unpaid dower is a debt of the husband's estate and passes to the wife's heirs if she dies.
